title: How to Trade Asia Using the TTrades Fractal Model
description: Learn how to trade Asia entries using positional entries and the 4-hour and 15-minute fractal model. Discover how higher timeframe bias, protected swings, and CISD work together before the expansion.

body.text: Introduction
The Asia session is often viewed as slow or difficult to trade, but under the right conditions it can provide high-quality entry opportunities before the main expansion of the day.
The key is understanding when an expansion is likely and choosing the correct execution model.

Within the fractal model, there are two primary ways to approach Asia entries. The first is through a positional entry when a higher timeframe protected swing is already in place. The second is by using a 4-hour and 15-minute fractal model to trade the developing daily wick. This guide explains when each approach should be used and why higher timeframe bias is the foundation of every Asia setup.
Not Every Asia Session Should Be Traded
Most Asia sessions are not worth trading.
The framework only looks for Asia entries when there is a reason to expect expansion. That generally occurs in one of two situations:
- A completed higher timeframe reversal suggests the next candle should expand.
- Price opens close to a draw on liquidity where expansion can begin immediately.
Without one of these conditions, there is no reason to force an entry simply because the Asia session is underway.
Higher Timeframe Bias Comes First
Every Asia trade begins with higher timeframe analysis.

A daily Candle 2 closure, combined with a confirmed change in state of delivery (CISD), creates the expectation that Candle 3 can expand. That expectation becomes the reason to look for opportunities during the Asia session rather than reacting to lower timeframe price movement alone.
The lower timeframe provides execution.
The higher timeframe provides the reason for the trade.
Option One: Positional Entries in Asia
The first approach is a positional entry.

If a protected swing has already formed before the new higher timeframe candle opens, that protected swing becomes the invalidation level. Rather than waiting for another confirmation that may never appear, the position can be established near the open of the higher timeframe candle while expecting the daily expansion to begin.
This approach is designed for situations where price may expand immediately without offering another retracement.
Option Two: The 4-Hour and 15-Minute Fractal Model
Not every setup is suitable for a positional entry.

If the structure is not strong enough before the daily open, waiting for a 4-hour Candle 2 closure provides additional confirmation. Once that higher timeframe confirmation forms, the 15-minute fractal model can be used to identify an intra-candle change in state of delivery and a new protected swing before entering.
Instead of anticipating the move, this approach waits for additional structure before looking for an entry.
Protected Swings Define Risk
Regardless of the execution method, every trade requires a logical invalidation.
Protected swings provide that level.
The protected swing provides the logical location for the stop loss because it is the level that should remain intact if the higher timeframe expectation is correct.
If that protected swing fails, the original idea for the trade is no longer valid.
Positional Entries Require Confidence in the Framework
A positional entry is not simply an early entry.
It is an execution technique built on a completed higher timeframe framework.
Without a clear bias, a confirmed Candle 2 closure, and a protected swing close to the higher timeframe open, there is no reason to enter positionally.
The framework determines when a positional entry makes sense.
It is never based on anticipation alone.
Reversal Days Need More Confirmation
Reversal setups require more confirmation than continuation trades

When trading a reversal day, additional confirmation such as SMT, an hourly change in state of delivery, and a 4-hour Candle 2 closure help strengthen the framework before looking for a 15-minute execution.
More confirmation reduces the likelihood of entering against the current price delivery before the reversal is confirmed.
Overnight Trades Should Not Be Overmanaged
One of the advantages of Asia entries is their simplicity.

Once the trade is planned, the stop loss and take-profit levels are already defined by the framework. Rather than managing every small fluctuation overnight, the position is allowed to either reach its target or invalidate naturally.
Good execution comes from planning the trade before entering it, not from reacting to every movement afterward.
Final Thoughts
Trading the Asia session is not about finding activity during quiet market hours.
It is about recognizing when the higher timeframe framework supports an expansion and choosing the correct execution model.
Sometimes that means entering positionally before the move begins.
Other times, it means waiting for the 4-hour Candle 2 closure to form before looking for a 15-minute Fractal Model entry.
In both cases, the higher timeframe provides the bias, protected swings define the risk, and the fractal model provides the framework for consistent execution.
